sources.title: Library of Congress Law Library, Treaty on the Creation of the Soviet Union
sources.note: Treaty adopted 30 December 1922 by Russia, Ukraine, Belarus and Transcaucasian federation; USSR did not immediately succeed empire and 1924 constitution followed.

sources.title: Russian Federal Archives, 1922 Declaration and Treaty of Formation
sources.note: Federal archive entry for 30 December 1922 formation documents and original Russian title Союза Советских Социалистических Республик; official state text is not all residents’ home language.

sources.title: Library of Congress, Internal Workings of the Soviet Union
sources.note: Archival exhibit covers 1928 industrialization, collectivization, 1932-33 famine, Great Terror, religious persecution, antisemitic campaign, 1986 Chornobyl disaster and perestroika.

sources.title: National Museum of the Holodomor, History of the Holodomor
sources.note: Ukrainian national museum frames the deliberately inflicted 1932-33 famine in Soviet Ukraine as genocide; important affected-community perspective.

sources.title: Library of Congress, 1932 Physician Report on Collectivization
sources.note: Translated 1932 physician report describes starving families and sick children in one Siberian collective-farm area; local testimony, not union-wide census.

sources.title: Library of Congress, Russian and Ukrainian Pamphlet Collection: Education
sources.note: Education documents show changing Soviet administration, methods and curricula 1917-1930s, including a 1933 Ukrainian secondary-school program.

sources.title: Library of Congress Federal Research Division, Soviet Union: A Country Study
sources.note: Late-Soviet country study sections on education, healthcare staff (many women physicians), rural access, employment and unequal access to scarce consumer goods; 1980s perspective.

sources.title: Hirshhorn Museum, Ilya Kabakov: Ten Characters
sources.note: Artist Kabakov recalls crowded communal Moscow apartment neighbors; artwork and memory are personal, not a population survey.

sources.title: Library of Congress digital book, Moving Toward Utopia: Soviet Housing
sources.note: Scholarly chapter describes communal apartments sharing kitchen, lavatory and bathroom and Khrushchev’s 1957 campaign for separate family apartments; urban examples, not universal.

sources.title: United States Holocaust Memorial Museum, Soviet Union and Eastern Front
sources.note: 1939 German-Soviet pact, 1941 Nazi invasion, war of annihilation, mass murder of Jews and other civilians, Soviet counteroffensive and 1945 victory.

sources.title: NASA, 60 Years Ago: Soviets Select Their First Cosmonauts
sources.note: Soviet cosmonaut training and engineering, 1960 Belka/Strelka animal flight, 1961 Gagarin first human spaceflight; many workers involved.

sources.title: NASA, Sputnik 1
sources.note: 1957 launch of first human-made Earth satellite; Soviet scientific and engineering achievement.

sources.title: Library of Congress, Chornobyl Nuclear Accident Archive Guide
sources.note: Archival trail includes pre-1986 construction-flaw memorandum, accident reports and later information-control documents; cite for 1986 accident and state secrecy.

sources.title: Library of Congress, Soviet Independent Press 1987-1992
sources.note: Independent print media rose during glasnost and perestroika beginning 1985; change in freedom of expression.

sources.title: U.S. State Department Office of the Historian, Collapse of the Soviet Union
sources.note: Republic independence movements, failed August 1991 coup, Gorbachev resignation and Soviet flag lowered 25 December; 15 independent republics emerged, no single replacement for peoples.

sources.title: United Nations Yearbook 1991, Former Soviet Republics
sources.note: 1991 UN account of constituent republics, independence and December Commonwealth of Independent States; not all republics followed identical transition.

proposedOverrides.summary: The Soviet Union was a multi-republic state founded in 1922. It industrialized rapidly, expanded schooling and healthcare and launched the first satellite and human spaceflight, while forced collectivization, famine, purges and wartime devastation caused immense suffering. Homes, languages and opportunities differed across republics. The union dissolved in 1991; its peoples and cultures continued in independent countries.
